body.cap: Mayor Oh Se-hoon welcomed the attendees at his speech at the opening ceremony of CES 2024, the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, held in Las Vegas on the 9th (local time). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Seoul City operated the largest-ever “Seoul Pavilion” at CES 2024, the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, for four days from January 9 (Tue) to 12 (Fri).

Mayor Oh Se-hoon, who visited the Seoul Pavilion on the 10th (local time), took the lead in networking with global companies, startups, governments, IT experts, and more, promoting Seoul’s smart city competitiveness and Korean companies on the world stage.

At the opening ceremony, Mayor Oh Se-hoon expressed satisfaction, stating, “Seoul City has continuously opened the Seoul Pavilion to enable our companies to participate in CES since 2020. This year, a total of 81 entities, the largest ever, participated through collaboration with 13 organizations, and two of them received the CES Best of Innovation Award.”

During his speech, Mayor Oh praised TopTable (AI-based personalized nutrition solution) and LordSystem (mobile passport), which received the CES Best of Innovation Award, granted to only 1% of participating companies at CES.

Mayor Oh emphasized the significance of the CES Innovation Award, saying, “This year, Seoul Pavilion received 2 Best Innovation Awards and 18 Innovation Awards. The CES Innovation Award acknowledges the technological capabilities of winning companies and serves as an important foundation for their growth.” He explained, “Among the 51 companies that participated in CES last year, 17 award-winning companies received KRW 36.5 billion in investments over the year, securing numerous overseas business opportunities and laying the foundation for rapid growth.”

body.cap: Mayor Oh Se-hoon, along with Kim Hyun-woo, CEO of Seoul Business Agency, and Gary Shapiro, CTA President, takes a commemorative photo at the opening ceremony of CES 2024, the world’s largest consumer electronics and IT exhibition, held in Las Vegas on the 9th at 10 a.m. (local time). | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Mayor Oh said he found the importance of opening the Seoul Pavilion through the CES Innovation Award. He stated, “In the future, Seoul City will spare no effort to support various aspects, including research and development, testbed provision, business development, and workspace support, to enable more innovative companies to grow.”

The 13 collaborating organizations participating in this year’s Seoul Pavilion include the Seoul Economic Promotion Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul AI Hub, Gwanak-gu, Korea University, Yonsei University, Sogang University, Hanyang University, Chung-Ang University, Konkuk University, Kookmin University, Kyung Hee University, and Ewha Womans University. CES 2024’s “Seoul Pavilion,” decorated in pink, is the largest-ever CES Seoul Pavilion, covering 670 square meters, and is located in the Eureka Park (Tech West), a national startup exhibition hall.

Mayor Oh Se-hoon remarked, “Seeing the CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion decorated in Seoul’s innate color, it seems like a pink-tinted future is guaranteed. I hope this CES participation will ensure a bright future for Korean companies.”

Furthermore, Mayor Oh had a luncheon meeting with representatives of award-winning companies to encourage companies that achieved good results with innovative technologies and products in the global investment environment. He listened to the voices of the industry regarding regulations and challenges faced during global expansion and business development. Especially in startups with new initiatives and technologies, Seoul City will expand its support to eliminate regulatory barriers that break the entrepreneurial spirit, actively serve as a platform for delivering suggestions to the central government, and actively suggest areas the central government needs to address.
